title: Glucose-HR coupling rigidity is timescale-selective: strongest at ultradian scales
statement: The diabetes-associated increase in glucose-HR coupling is not uniform across timescales. It is strongest at ultradian frequencies (1-4 hour oscillations corresponding to meal-driven glucose excursions and postprandial autonomic responses), weaker at high-frequency scales (<30 min, dominated by activity artifacts and HR noise), and absent or reversed at circadian scales (>8h, reflecting preserved gross day-night organization). This predicts that wavelet coherence between glucose and HR at 1-4h periods will show a larger diabetes severity gradient (Cohen's d > 0.6) than coherence at <30min or >8h periods.
mechanism: Postprandial glucose excursions trigger sympathetic activation and HR acceleration through hepato-portal glucose sensing, incretin-mediated vagal signaling, and direct central glucose sensing. In healthy physiology, these excursions are buffered by intact baroreflexes and parasympathetic counterregulation, limiting glucose-HR coherence to brief postprandial windows. In diabetes, impaired autonomic buffering (vagal denervation progresses before sympathetic) allows glucose excursions to drive HR more persistently at 1-4h meal timescales. However, the gross circadian organization of HR (sleep-related bradycardia, daytime tachycardia) is preserved until advanced autonomic neuropathy, so circadian-scale coherence should not differ as strongly. Sub-30-minute fluctuations are dominated by HR noise from posture and activity rather than glucose-driven physiology.
predictions: Wavelet coherence at 1-4h periods shows the largest Cohen's d (>0.6) for healthy-vs-insulin contrast, exceeding the broadband zero-lag correlation effect (d=0.585)
Coherence at <30min periods shows Cohen's d < 0.2 (negative control: noise-dominated scale)
Coherence at >8h circadian periods shows Cohen's d < 0.3 (preserved gross day-night organization)
The 1-4h coherence effect survives adjustment for HbA1c, BMI, mean glucose, mean HR, and activity volume
Within the insulin-dependent group, 1-4h coherence correlates positively with HOMA-IR (r > 0.15)

literature.title: Glucose and unstructured physical activity coupling during sleep and wake in young adults with type 1 diabetes
literature.key_finding: Wavelet coherence between glucose and physical activity was strongest at 120-340 min periods (ultradian timescale) with significant circadian modulation of coupling strength.
literature.relevance: Demonstrates that glucose-activity coupling is timescale-selective in T1D; we hypothesize glucose-HR coupling in T2D has analogous scale dependence.

literature.title: Decreased complexity of glucose dynamics in diabetes: evidence from multiscale entropy analysis of continuous glucose monitoring system data
literature.journal: American Journal of Physiology - Endocrinology and Metabolism
literature.key_finding: Glucose complexity loss in diabetes is scale-dependent, most prominent at scales from 5 min to 5 hours, not explained by mean/variance differences.
literature.relevance: Establishes that diabetes alters glucose dynamics in a scale-dependent manner, supporting the hypothesis that coupling changes are also scale-selective.

literature.title: Network physiology reveals relations between network topology and physiological function
literature.key_finding: Inter-organ coupling strength and topology depend on physiological state (sleep stage) and operate at specific timescales.
literature.relevance: Foundational network physiology framework predicting that coupling breakdown is scale-specific, not broadband.

feasibility.statistical_power: N~1900 with 10-day window; well-powered for d>0.3 across frequency bands
key_challenges: Morlet wavelet coherence requires sufficient time-series length for low-frequency bands
Need cone-of-influence correction for edge effects at multi-day boundaries
dataset_limitations: Garmin HR is not beat-to-beat; high-frequency HR dynamics are smoothed
No medication data to adjust for beta-blocker dampening of HR response
10-day window limits precision of >8h frequency estimates

test_plan.primary_method: Continuous wavelet transform coherence (Morlet wavelet, omega0=6) between glucose and HR, averaged over the 10-day window, computed at 5 frequency bands: <30min, 30-60min, 1-2h, 2-4h, 4-8h, >8h
implementation_steps: Step 1: Load aligned 5-min glucose and HR time series per participant
Step 2: Apply continuous wavelet transform (CWT) with Morlet wavelet to both signals
Step 3: Compute wavelet coherence (WCO) and phase as a function of time and period
Step 4: Average WCO within 6 predefined period bands across time, excluding cone of influence
Step 5: Extract per-participant band-specific mean coherence and mean phase angle
Step 6: Test group differences (Kruskal-Wallis, trend test) for each band separately
Step 7: Compare Cohen's d across bands to test scale-selectivity prediction
Step 8: Run sensitivity models adjusting for age, site, HbA1c, BMI, mean glucose, mean HR
test_plan.expected_effect_size: Cohen's d 0.6-0.8 at 1-4h band; d < 0.2 at <30min band
test_plan.success_criterion: Statistically significant interaction between frequency band and diabetes severity, with 1-4h band showing largest group difference
test_plan.refutation_criterion: If coupling increase is uniform across all frequency bands (no band x group interaction), the timescale-selectivity claim fails. If <30min band shows equal or larger d than 1-4h band, the mechanism is non-specific.
sensitivity_checks: Stratify by awake/sleep to test circadian modulation of the band-specific effect
Bootstrap 1000x per-participant coherence estimates for CI
Compare Morlet vs. Paul wavelet to assess wavelet choice sensitivity
Exclude participants with <5 days of aligned data
secondary_methods: Hilbert transform instantaneous phase for narrowband signals

results.interpretation: Timescale selectivity is strongly confirmed -- broadband coupling (d=0.06, n.s.) masks a frequency-dependent effect where short-period coherence (30min-2h) DECREASES while long-period coherence (2-8h) INCREASES with diabetes severity. This is more interesting than the simple prediction: diabetes doesn't uniformly increase coupling. It shifts the dominant coupling timescale toward slower oscillations, consistent with impaired fast autonomic buffering (parasympathetic) while metabolic-level coupling at meal/hormonal timescales (2-8h) strengthens. The flipped directionality around 2h is the key finding.
results.surprise: The short-period coupling DECREASES -- opposite to the overall broadband increase found in H-MIG01. This means the broadband glucose-HR correlation increase is driven entirely by slow (>2h) coupling, while fast coupling actually breaks down.
results.method_used: Welch spectral coherence at 4 frequency bands (30-60min, 1-2h, 2-4h, 4-8h) + Kruskal-Wallis + OLS severity trend adjusted for age/site

sensitivity_checks.name: Broadband coherence (non-specific)
sensitivity_checks.details: Broadband d=0.06 is non-significant. Confirms timescale selectivity.

sensitivity_checks.name: Short-period negative control
sensitivity_checks.details: 30-60min and 1-2h show DECREASED coherence (d=-0.22, -0.17). Opposite direction to prediction.

issues: The 10-day window provides only ~2.5 full cycles at the >8h band, making circadian-scale coherence estimates unreliable and likely inflating confidence intervals. The cone-of-influence will eat a large fraction of usable data at these long periods.

The <30min negative control is confounded by Garmin HR smoothing: Garmin averages HR at 1-5 min resolution, so any sub-30min coherence is mechanically attenuated regardless of physiology. This makes the negative control trivially satisfied.

No meal timing data means the 1-4h band coherence cannot be attributed to meal-driven excursions specifically. It could reflect ultradian hormonal oscillations (cortisol, GH) that happen to peak at similar frequencies.
Adjusting for HbA1c AND mean glucose is borderline redundant; both capture glycemic level and their joint inclusion may create collinearity problems.
confounders_missed: Beta-blocker use (redacted): dampens HR oscillations across all timescales, could selectively reduce 1-4h coherence in medicated participants
Meal frequency/regularity: participants who eat on rigid schedules vs. grazing will have different ultradian glucose periodicity regardless of disease state
Physical fitness level: affects autonomic tone and HR dynamics at all timescales
suggestions: Drop the >8h band analysis entirely -- 10 days is insufficient for circadian coherence estimates. Focus on the 30min-8h range where statistical power is adequate.
Replace the <30min negative control with a surrogate-based test (time-shifted glucose vs real HR) at 1-4h band, which is a stronger null test that is not confounded by Garmin smoothing.
Report both raw and activity-conditioned coherence at each band to separate activity-driven from autonomic-driven coupling.
Pre-register that the 1-4h band d must exceed 1.2x the broadband d (not just be 'larger'), giving a quantitative bar for timescale selectivity.

notes: This decomposes the broadband coupling finding (H-MIG01) by frequency. If confirmed, the 1-4h band coherence becomes a more mechanistically specific biomarker than the broadband correlation.
